Present petition has been filed seeking inter-alia quashing of letter dated 03rd August, 2023 issued by respondent no.3, pertaining to a joint survey for handing over the physical possession of the land parcels to Respondent no. 2, which according to the petitioner, belongs to the petitioner trust.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been carrying out its activities from a superstructure erected upon a piece of land admeasuring 3 bighas 7 biswa situated at Plot D in Khasra No. 57, Village Behlolpur Khadar, New Delhi - 110013, popularly identified as Jain This is a digitally signed order.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner has drawn the attention of this Court to Land Acquisition Award no. 15/92-93 dated 19th June, 1992.

He relies upon the following portion of the award, wherein it is stated that certain area has been left out from acquisition:
"xxx xxx xxx COMPENSATION OF TREES AND STRUCTURE

inviting applications from institutions existing before 01st January, 2006, which were engaged in Cultural, Religious, Spiritual, Healthcare, and Education Services.
It is submitted that the petitioner also submitted an application with regard thereto on 09th June, 2008.

sentences.text: 7. It is submitted that the petitioner is also a bonafide institution engaged in rendering Cultural, Religious, Spiritual, Health Care and Education Services.

8. Learned Senior Counsel for petitioner further submits that the petitioner recently came to know about the letter dated 03rd August, 2023 issued by the respondent no.2 pertaining to joint survey for handing over the physical possession of the land parcels.
It is submitted that the aforesaid letter stands on a factually incorrect foundation and poses a great threat to legally vested rights of the petitioner.

9. It is submitted that the action of the respondents as reflected in the letter dated 03rd August, 2023 is contrary to the stated policy of the respondents in the Zonal Manav Mandir Mission Trust vs Union Of India & Ors on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47092081/

10. Per contra, learned Standing Counsel for respondent no. 2-DDA draws the attention of this Court to the Judgment dated 27th April, 2015 passed by Division Bench of this Court in W.P.(C) 7660/2014.

She submits that by the aforesaid judgment, petitioner had obtained orders in his favour wherein the Division Bench had held that the petitioner was entitled to a declaration that the acquisition proceedings in respect of the said land are deemed to have lapsed.

"Leave granted.

The challenge in the present appeal is to an order passed by the High Court on 27.04.2015, whereby the respondent-writ petitioner was given the benefit of Section 24(2) of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act, 2013 and consequently, a direction was issued that the acquisition proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 are deemed

sentences.text: However, the learned counsel for the respondent wishes to withdraw the writ petition filed before the High Court itself because the writ petitioner is running old age home, orphanage, and a temple on a land admeasuring 3 Bighas and 7 Biswas, the land, which is the subject matter of acquisition, to seek redressal of his grievances in. accordance with law.
In view of above, the appeal is allowed.
The writ petition filed before the High Court is dismissed as withdrawn, as sought for.

sentences.text: By relying upon the aforesaid order, it is submitted that the petitioner had withdrawn his petition and the appeal of the DDA had been allowed, meaning thereby that the acquisition of the land of the petitioner also stood sustained.
Thus, she submits that the matter has been settled right up to the Supreme Court.
14. This Court finds force in the submissions made by the learned Standing Counsel for DDA.

However, perusal of the Award dated 19th June, 1992, which has been reproduced as aforesaid,
shows that certain portions of Khasra Nos. 56 and 57 were left out of acquisition. The petitioner claims to be in possession of the Khasra No. 57 Min.

15. Learned Standing Counsel for DDA at this stage submits that the Land Acquisition Collector ("LAC") would be a necessary party, as the requisite records would be with the LAC.
16. Considering the submission as aforesaid, this Court is of the view that the LAC is a necessary party in the present proceedings.
Accordingly, Land Acquisition Collector ("LAC"), District South-East is impleaded as respondent no. 5 in the present petition.
17. Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, who is present in court, is requested to appear on behalf of newly impleaded respondent.
The petitioner shall provide a full copy of the present petition to the learned counsel for LAC within a period of one day.

18. The DDA as well as LAC, District South-East are directed to apprise the court as regards the acquisition of land pursuant to Award No. 15/92-93 dated 19th June, 1992 with respect to village Behlolpur Khadar.

They are further directed to file requisite documents along with affidavit within a period of 10 days, to indicate as to whether the land, which is in occupation of the petitioner, is part of the acquired land as per the aforesaid Award.

It is further directed that both DDA and LAC,
District South-East shall also identify the specific area which has been left out of the acquisition, as per the aforesaid Award, if any.

19. Let amended memo of parties be filed within a period of one week from today.
20.
Re- notify on 06th March, 2024.
